summary.headline: Asahi Songwon Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA rose 30.2% YoY to Rs 23 crore, with margin at 15.6% on price pass-through in Blue pigments.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q4 FY26 revenue was Rs 144 crore, up 19.4% QoQ, with EBITDA of Rs 23 crore (15.6% margin vs 8.58% in Q3 and 11.53% in Q4 FY25) and PAT of Rs 10.82 crore. For FY26, revenue fell 4.78% to Rs 535.48 crore while PAT rose 5.48% to Rs 17.78 crore. Management attributed the margin recovery mainly to raw-material price pass-through and operational efficiencies in Blue pigments, with a small inventory gain, and said the API price decline of the prior three years has reversed. Gokul Jaykrishna handed day-to-day CEO duties to his son Arjun Jaykrishna, while remaining Managing Director.

segments.name: Blue pigment (standalone, ATC Dahej)
segments.commentary: Revenue and profitability improved QoQ on stronger realisation with modest volume growth. Gross margin rose to about 34% from about 29% QoQ; management cited price pass-through, operating efficiencies and a marginal inventory gain. Management said utilisation is about 80-85% and no capex is planned for capacity.

segments.name: AZO pigments (subsidiary ATC)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive and cash break-even reached. FY26 revenue Rs 78 crore with PBT loss of Rs 2.42 crore; management expects PBT break-even in FY27. Capacity is 2,400 tpa, utilisation about 65% per management, with a planned Rs 10-15 crore brownfield expansion to about 1.5x once utilisation reaches 75-85%.

segments.name: API (subsidiary Atlas, Chattral plant)
segments.commentary: Full-year EBITDA positive. Volumes grew about 18% CAGR over three years, but realisations fell 40-45% since acquisition; Pregabalin prices are about 15% above the bottom. Pregabalin is 60-70% of API business. Chattral intermediates run at about 60-70% and finished APIs at about 30%. Q4 API revenue was reported as about Rs 30 crore with EBIT of about 10%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects Q1 FY27 EBITDA across all three segments to at least maintain Q4 FY26 margins, with an aim to improve.

Blue standalone: management said peak EBITDA of about Rs 50-55 crore is the goal for FY27 if prices hold, on about Rs 400 crore revenue at 13-14% margin (analyst's framing, accepted as a goal, not a formal guide).

Long-term margin targets: about 13% EBITDA for AZO and 15-16% for API; Mitesh Patel said Chattral and Atlas could reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex, at 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years.
CEP certification for Pregabalin expected by end of FY27 (current financial year), seen as a driver of volume and export access.
Management aims for Rs 1,000 crore group revenue within the next few years, with priority on sustaining revenue first.
capex_capacity: AZO capacity 2,400 tpa; brownfield expansion of about Rs 10-15 crore (plant and machinery only) to lift capacity to about 1.5x, triggered at 75-85% utilisation, expected within 3-4 quarters and funded by internal accruals.
Blue: no capex planned for capacity; incremental gains expected from debottlenecking and efficiency projects.
Chattral: intermediates about 60-70% utilised; finished API utilisation about 30%, which management sees as the key lever for fixed-asset turnover.
Peak debt was Rs 220 crore after the completed four-year capex cycle; debt is falling faster than internal estimates.
demand_pricing: Blue pricing is set quarterly with MNC customers; Q4 benefit was partly locked in, so further benefit expected in Q1 and Q2. Mitesh Patel put the price increase at about 20%, and management said prices across pigments and crude rose meaningfully on raw-material tightness.
Management said China raised prices about 30-40% due to lower export incentives and VAT rebates, roughly doubled ocean freight and higher crude-linked raw material costs.

US tariffs hit AZO and Blue exports, including via India-made value-added products; US business has revived since tariffs eased but has not returned to normal. AZO export customers have restarted testing.
Management said Europe remains in a structural slowdown; India remains the main AZO growth market.
Management says the cyclical slowdown appears to be bottoming, and no new pigment capacity is expected in the industry.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA gain came from raw-material price pass-through, and does it reverse if raw material prices fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun Jaykrishna said the strategy was to pass through as much raw-material inflation as possible via long-term supplier and customer relationships. He did not quantify the split and said revenue was under pressure while the bottom line held.

qa_highlights.question: Blue gross margin rose from about 29% to 34% QoQ. Is there inventory gain, and how do margins return to 35-38%?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said margins reflect internal strategy, some inventory addition, and operating efficiencies. Gokul Jaykrishna later put the inventory gain as marginal, since the company held finished goods bought before the war.

qa_highlights.question: Did the Blue power and fuel cost fall to under 5% of sales in Q4 because of a one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Arjun said a one-time receipt of renewable-energy billing rebate, pending for two years, drove the drop. Management expects power and fuel as a percentage of sales to be lower than before but not at Q4 levels every quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is AZO FY26 revenue and PBT, and will it break even in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Nupur (company) said FY26 AZO revenue was Rs 78 crore and PBT was Rs (-2.42) crore. Management said it expects PBT break-even in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Standalone Blue utilisation and possible FY27 EBITDA of Rs 50-55 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Gokul Jaykrishna corrected the analyst's 60% figure, saying Blue runs at about 80-85%. He called Rs 50-55 crore peak potential and the goal for FY27. Mitesh Patel put Blue price increases at about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Subsidiaries: peak revenue and EBITDA potential at Atlas and Chattral?
qa_highlights.answer: Mitesh Patel said the two facilities can reach Rs 250-280 crore turnover at peak with no capex and 15-16% EBITDA margin within 2-3 years. Arjun said API EBITDA depends on pricing, and management said the subsidiaries could reach about Rs 50 crore EBITDA at peak.

risks_watch: Q4 margin gains were partly one-off: a renewable-energy rebate lowered Blue power and fuel costs, and an inventory gain contributed. Q1 FY27 is the test.
Pricing is volatile: management says there is no stability in prices or the business environment; a reversal of raw-material inflation could compress margins.
API utilisation at Chattral finished products is about 30%, and the company has not yet hired senior business development or marketing leadership; a senior hire is expected in the next quarter.
FY26 consolidated revenue fell 4.78% and EBITDA 6.12%; FY26 net margin about 3.3%. AZO and API are still loss-making or marginal, so consolidation depends on Blue.
CEP certification for Pregabalin (targeted by end FY27) and AZO export approvals in the US and Europe remain unconfirmed timelines.
Leadership transition: Gokul Jaykrishna stepped down as CEO and Arjun Jaykrishna took over as CEO.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Q4 and the Blue business, but cautious on the subsidiaries and the wider market. Management was candid that AZO and API margins are far from targets and that the environment is volatile, and it avoided quantifying the inventory gain, the price pass-through split and the Blue revenue mix. Some answers were loose or corrected on the call.
key_quotes: The strategy and implementation we have been working on is going to strongly position us in the Blue business to continue to perform at a good level in the coming quarters and year as well.

So, the crude and the Pigment, I think both would be subs tantial contributors and they will be in the coming future, but I will request, if it is okay, that we do not share the exact breakup just for business.
The API business has delivered consistent volumetric growth continuously of 3 years.
We are far from that. And we need to make serious strategic decisions as well as good business operational moves to reach this.
